The '''Professor of Logic and Rhetoric''' is a professorship at the [[University of Glasgow]]. The Nova Erectio of [[King James VI of Scotland]] shared the teaching of [[moral philosophy]], logic and natural philosophy among the Regents.<ref>[https://www.gla.ac.uk/media/Media_94581_smxx.pdf  University of Glasgow website, ''A Brief History'' (page 2)]</ref>

In 1727, separate chairs were instituted, one of which was the Chair of Logic and Rhetoric.<ref>[https://archiveshub.jisc.ac.uk/search/archives/5423a1c4-bcfe-3c21-8dcd-0ebf353a9207?component=6f7821bb-5c4d-3341-adb7-371b83480cdb  JISC Archive website, ''Records of the University of Glasgow, Scotland: Department of Applied Physics'']</ref>

==Holders of the Chair of Logic and Rhetoric==
* John Loudon MA (1727)
* [[Adam Smith]] MA LLD (1751) Later [[Professor of Moral Philosophy, Glasgow|Professor of Moral Philosophy]] and Rector 
* James Clow MA (1752)
* [[George Jardine]] MA (1774)
* [[Robert Buchanan (playwright)|Robert Buchanan]] MA LLD (1827)
* [[John Veitch (poet)|John Veitch]] MA LLD (1864)
* [[Robert Adamson (philosopher)|Robert Adamson]] MA LLD (1895)
* Robert Latta MA DPhil LLD (1902)
* Archibald Allan Bowman MA LittD (1925) Later Professor of Moral Philosophy
* [[Herbert James Paton]] MA DLitt (1927)
* Charles Arthur Campbell MA DLitt (1938)
* Rodney Julian Hurst MA (1961–1981)
* [[Alexander Broadie]] MA PhD DLitt FRSE FBA (1995)
* Fraser MacBride MA MPhil PhD (2013–16)
* Jack Lyons BA PhD (2020-)<ref>[https://www.gla.ac.uk/subjects/philosophy/staff/  University of Glasgow website, ''Philosophy staff'', retrieved 11 December 2024]</ref>
